## Grading

| Component | Weight | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Attendance | 5% | Checked every session |
| In-class exercises (14) | 10% | Good-faith completion; lowest 2 dropped |
| Weekly exercises (12) | 35% | Autograded on GitHub; lowest 2 dropped |
| In-class quizzes (5) | 20% | Weeks 3, 6, 9, 11, 13; no AI; lowest dropped |
| Final individual project | 30% | Quarto report + video walkthrough + AI appendix |

**Grading scale (graduate).** A: 94–100 · A−: 90–93 · B+: 87–89 · B: 83–86 ·
B−: 80–82 · C+: 77–79 · C: 73–76 · C−: 70–72 · F: below 70

## Assessments in brief

**Weekly exercises** are released before class on Wednesdays in Weeks 1–12
and due 11:59 PM the following Wednesday. They are distributed and submitted
through GitHub; an autograder reports which questions pass every time you push,
and you may resubmit freely before the deadline. Late: 20% penalty within 24h,
40% within 48h, zero after that.


**In-class quizzes** (15 minutes, five total: Weeks 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) are
paper-based hand-fluency checks completed individually without laptops, phones,
or AI assistance during the last 20 minutes of class. To provide flexibility for
unexpected illness or travel, your **lowest quiz score is automatically dropped**
(the best 4 of 5 count, 3.75% each, 15% total).


**The final project** is an individual analysis of a public-health dataset:
a reproducible Quarto report in a GitHub repository, a 5-minute recorded video
walkthrough, and an AI-use appendix. Released Week 10, due 11:59 PM December
16. No late submissions.

## Software (all free)

R, RStudio, Quarto, Git, and a free GitHub account. Free-tier AI chatbots are
sufficient for all coursework. No purchases are required.
